dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4601.text: A building leaning downward. Formed from 宀, with 執 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4602.text: A temple honoring ancestors. Formed from 宀 and 示.

shuowen:4603.text: The ancestral tablet and its stone shrine in a temple. Formed from 宀, with 主 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4604.text: The utmost covering of boats and carriages. Formed from 宀, with 由 indicating the sound; the exact sense of 所極覆 is uncertain.

shuowen:4605.text: To place or set down. Formed from 宀, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4606.text: Counties within the royal domain’s boundary. Formed from 宀, with 瞏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4607.text: Sharing the same territory is 寀. Formed from 宀, with 采 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4608.text: A chamber. Formed from 宀, with abbreviated 躳 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 宮.

shuowen:4609.text: A market settlement. Formed from 宮, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4610.text: The spinal bones. Pictographic. Long ago Taiyue served Yu as his heart-and-backbone minister, and was therefore enfeoffed as Marquis of Lü. All characters in this group follow 呂.

shuowen:4611.text: The body. Formed from 身 and 呂.

shuowen:4612.text: An earthen chamber. Formed from 宀, with 八 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 穴.

shuowen:4613.text: Northern people use a hollow in the ground as an earthen dwelling, called 𥥊戶. Formed from 穴, with 皿 indicating the sound. Read like 猛.

shuowen:4614.text: An underground chamber. Formed from 穴, with 音 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4615.text: A furnace for firing tiles. Formed from 穴, with 羔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4616.text: An underground chamber. Formed from 穴, with 復 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Dig chambers, dig caves.”

shuowen:4617.text: A cooking stove. Formed from 穴, with abbreviated 鼀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4618.text: The opening in a steaming vessel. Formed from 穴, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4619.text: Deep. Another explanation: a stove’s chimney. Formed from 穴, 火 and abbreviated 求.

shuowen:4620.text: To pass through. Formed from 牙 inside 穴.

shuowen:4621.text: To pierce through. Formed from 穴, with 尞 indicating the sound. The Analects mentions Gongbo Liao, 公伯竂.

shuowen:4622.text: To pierce through. Formed from 穴, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4623.text: To gouge deeply. Formed from 穴 and 抉.

shuowen:4624.text: A hollow opening. Formed from 穴, with abbreviated 瀆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4625.text: A hollow appearance. Formed from 穴, with 矞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4626.text: A hollow: a nest in a hole is 窠, one in a tree 巢. Formed from 穴, with 果 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4627.text: A hole passing through. Formed from 穴, with 怱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4628.text: Sunken and sloping: low. Formed from 穴, with 瓜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4629.text: An opening. Formed from 穴, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4630.text: A hole or opening. Formed from 穴, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4631.text: Empty. Formed from 穴, with 巠 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The jar is empty.”

shuowen:4632.text: A large hollow. Formed from 穴, with 乙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4633.text: Sunken or hollow, 污窬. Formed from 穴, with 㼌 indicating the sound. Shuofang has Yuhun County, 窳渾.

shuowen:4634.text: A small pit inside a pit. Formed from 穴 and 臽; 臽 also indicates the sound. The Changes says: “Entering the pit within the pit.” Another explanation: entering from the side.

shuowen:4635.text: An underground store, 窖. Formed from 穴, with 卯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4636.text: To store underground. Formed from 穴, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4637.text: To cut through a wooden door. Formed from 穴, with 俞 indicating the sound. Another explanation: hollow inside.

shuowen:4638.text: 窵窅, deep. Formed from 穴, with 鳥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4639.text: To look through a small opening. Formed from 穴, with 規 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4640.text: To look straight. Formed from looking straight, 正見, within 穴; 正 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:4641.text: To see within a hole. Formed from 穴, with 叕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4642.text: The appearance of something inside a hole. Formed from 出 within 穴.

shuowen:4643.text: To fill or block. Formed from 穴, with 眞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4644.text: To block. Formed from 穴, with 至 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4645.text: A dog suddenly emerging from a hole. Formed from 犬 inside 穴. Another explanation: slippery.

shuowen:4646.text: To hide. Formed from 鼠 inside 穴.

shuowen:4647.text: To emerge suddenly from a hole. Formed from 穴, with 卒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4648.text: Pressed or constrained. Formed from 穴, with 君 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4649.text: Deep and extending to the utmost. Formed from 穴, with 兆 indicating the sound. Read like 挑.

shuowen:4650.text: At an end or exhausted. Formed from 穴, with 弓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4651.text: To reach the end. Formed from 穴, with 九 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4652.text: The utmost limit. Formed from 穴, with 躳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4653.text: Dark. Formed from 穴, with 㫐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4654.text: 䆞窔, deep. Formed from 穴, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4655.text: Deep and distant. Formed from 穴, with 遂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4656.text: Deep and distant. Formed from 穴, with 幼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4657.text: 杳窱, dim and deep. Formed from 穴, with 條 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4658.text: To dig into the ground. Formed from 穴, with 毳 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a small mouse. The Rites of Zhou says: “For a great funeral, first dig the grave.”

shuowen:4659.text: To lower a coffin in burial. Formed from 穴, with 乏 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “At the lowering, hold the axe.”

shuowen:4660.text: The deep night of burial. Formed from 穴, with 屯 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “In the long darkness of burial, follow the former ruler underground.”

shuowen:4661.text: The burial darkness, 窀穸. Formed from 穴, with 夕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4662.text: Entering a vessel and puncturing a point is called 䆘. Formed from 穴, with 甲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4663.text: Having awareness while asleep. Formed from 宀 and 疒, with 夢 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “By the sun, moon, stars and constellations divine the fortune of six dreams: regular, startling, thought-induced, waking, joyful and fearful dreams.” All characters in this group follow 㝱.

shuowen:4664.text: To lie ill. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with abbreviated 练 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4665.text: To lie asleep. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 未 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4666.text: Waking from sleep and finding the dream confirmed is 寤. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 吾 indicating the sound. Another explanation: seeing something by day and dreaming of it at night.

shuowen:4667.text: Chu people call sleeping 𡫽. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 女 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4668.text: Sleeping without yet having enough. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 米 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4669.text: To sleep soundly. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 水 indicating the sound. Read like 悸.

shuowen:4670.text: An illness of being startled while lying asleep. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4671.text: To speak with eyes closed in sleep. Formed from abbreviated 㝱, with 臬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4672.text: To start in sleep. Another explanation: a child crying 寣寣. Another: calling to one another, in Henei speech. Formed from abbreviated 㝱 and 言.

shuowen:4673.text: To lean. When a person is ill, this depicts leaning against a support. All characters in this group follow 疒.

shuowen:4674.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 矢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4675.text: Illness or pain. Formed from 疒, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4676.text: An illness becoming worse. Formed from 疒, with 丙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4677.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 鬼 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Like that diseased tree.” Another explanation: a swelling protruding to the side.

shuowen:4678.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 可 indicating the sound. The Five Phases Commentary says: “Then there are ailments of the mouth.”

shuowen:4679.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 甫 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “My servant is ill.”

shuowen:4680.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4681.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 祭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4682.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 眞 indicating the sound. Another explanation: abdominal swelling.

shuowen:4683.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 莫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4684.text: Cramping in the abdomen. Formed from 疒, with 丩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4685.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 員 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4686.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 閒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4687.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 出 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4688.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4689.text: An enduring illness. Formed from 疒, with 發 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4690.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 者 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “My horse is ill.”

shuowen:4691.text: Illness. Formed from 疒, with 從 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4692.text: An illness of cold. Formed from 疒, with 辛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4693.text: Headache. Formed from 疒, with 或 indicating the sound. Read like 洫 in 溝洫.

shuowen:4694.text: Aching and pain in the head. Formed from 疒, with 肖 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “In spring there are aching head ailments.”

shuowen:4695.text: A sore on the head. Formed from 疒, with 匕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4696.text: A wound or sore on the head. Formed from 疒, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4697.text: A sore, 瘍. Formed from 疒, with 羊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4698.text: An eye disease. Another explanation: harmful qi adhering to the body. Another: an eroding sore. Formed from 疒, with 馬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4699.text: A dispersed or broken voice; the gloss 散聲 is uncertain. Formed from 疒, with 斯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4700.text: A crooked mouth. Formed from 疒, with 爲 indicating the sound.
